article.title: Google DeepMind Launches WeatherNext 3, Cutting Forecast Grids to 5 Kilometers With Hourly Updates
article.summary: WeatherNext 3 trains on live satellite data instead of lagging weather-model outputs, cutting CRPS precipitation error up to 60% and rolling out across Search, Maps, and Gemini.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

Google DeepMind and Google Research on September 3 introduced WeatherNext 3, which the companies describe as their most advanced and accurate global weather model to date, according to [Google](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-deepmind/introducing-weathernext-3/). The model is rolling out across Google Search, the Gemini app, Google Maps, and Google Cloud, according to [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/03/googles-latest-ai-weather-model-gives-you-no-excuse-to-forget-your-umbrella/).

## What We Know

- WeatherNext 3 resolves key surface variables like temperature and moisture at a 5-kilometer resolution, other surface variables at 10 kilometers, and atmospheric variables such as wind speed at 25 kilometers, according to [Google](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-deepmind/introducing-weathernext-3/). That is roughly five times sharper than its predecessor, WeatherNext 2, which produced forecasts on a 25-kilometer grid in 6-hour increments, per the same source.
- The new model generates a fresh forecast every hour, compared with the 6-hour update cycle of WeatherNext 2, according to [Google](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-deepmind/introducing-weathernext-3/).
- The architectural shift behind the gains: most AI weather models, including WeatherNext 2, train on data produced by numerical weather prediction (NWP) systems — supercomputer-driven physics simulations that carry a six-hour data lag, according to [Google](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-deepmind/introducing-weathernext-3/). WeatherNext 3 instead ingests live, global geostationary satellite data directly, and trains on sparse weather station observations to build 5-kilometer global forecasts that account for local topography, per the same source.
- On precipitation, Google reports a Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS) improvement of up to 60% against NASA's IMERG satellite precipitation dataset, 30% against the MRMS radar dataset, and 10% against rain-gauge measurements at early lead times, according to [Google](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-deepmind/introducing-weathernext-3/). For forecasts a day or more out, the company says people will see up to 50% more accurate precipitation predictions, with the largest gains in regions where forecasting has historically been less reliable.
- Google says WeatherNext 3 has roughly 2.4 times as many parameters as its predecessor, according to [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/03/googles-latest-ai-weather-model-gives-you-no-excuse-to-forget-your-umbrella/).
- The model also adds forecasts built for renewable energy: 100-meter wind speeds at roughly turbine height for wind-power output, plus high-resolution cloud cover and solar radiation levels for solar farms, according to [Google](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-deepmind/introducing-weathernext-3/).
- Google positions the higher-resolution forecasts as particularly significant for Latin America, Africa, and Asia-Pacific, regions it says have historically been underserved by high-resolution forecasting because of the computing cost of traditional regional models, according to [Google](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-deepmind/introducing-weathernext-3/).
- WeatherNext 3 began powering weather features inside Google Search, the Gemini app, Google Maps, the Google Maps Platform Weather API, and Google Earth Engine starting the day of the announcement, according to [Google](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-deepmind/introducing-weathernext-3/). Researchers, developers, and businesses can also query the data through BigQuery and Earth Engine or bulk-download it from Google Cloud Storage, per the same source.
- [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/03/googles-latest-ai-weather-model-gives-you-no-excuse-to-forget-your-umbrella/) reports the model outperforms competing deep-learning weather systems and traditional government forecasts, and that it will integrate into Search, Maps, and Gemini as well as become available on Google Cloud.

## What We Don't Know

Google's announcement does not disclose the model's exact parameter count, only the roughly 2.4x increase reported by TechCrunch relative to WeatherNext 2. Neither source specifies how WeatherNext 3 performs head-to-head against named competing systems from other AI labs or national weather services, beyond the general framing that it outperforms them.

## Analysis

The core change Google is emphasizing is training data, not just model size. Shifting from numerical-weather-prediction outputs — which lag live conditions by up to six hours — to direct ingestion of satellite and weather-station observations is what the company credits for both the higher spatial resolution and the hourly update cycle. Whether that architecture holds its accuracy advantage as it scales to more regions and longer forecast horizons will depend on independent evaluation over time, beyond the initial comparisons Google has published.
